claims.claim: The arbitrary-palette premise is equivalent to a finite palette-free pairing certificate.
claims.evidence: From a valid coloring, the three neighbors of each vertex have a unique repeated-color pair and a singleton. Every generated equivalence joins equally colored vertices, so neither an edge nor a local pair–singleton constraint is collapsed. Conversely, coloring each equivalence class separately makes every edge proper and gives each neighborhood the two distinct class colors [a_v]=[b_v] and [t_v]. There are at most |V(G)| classes, so the certificate is finite.
claims.search_method: Direct proof audit of both implications and all feasibility conditions.

claims.claim: For a feasible pairing P, the minimum number of colors among valid colorings realizing P is exactly the chromatic number of an explicit quotient graph Q_P.
claims.evidence: Every coloring realizing P is constant on the generated equivalence classes. Its necessary inequalities are exactly the quotient edges induced by graph edges and pair–singleton constraints, so it descends to a proper coloring of Q_P. Conversely, every proper coloring of Q_P lifts to a proper coloring of G realizing P and having exactly two neighborhood colors. The descent and lift retain the number of used colors, proving equality of the minima.
claims.search_method: Direct proof audit of descent, lift, and preservation of color count.

claims.claim: The target is equivalent to: whenever G has one feasible pairing, it has a feasible pairing P with χ(Q_P)≤4.
claims.evidence: Claim 0 identifies the target premise with existence of a feasible pairing, and claim 1 identifies a four-color solution realizing P with χ(Q_P)≤4. Conversely, any target four-coloring supplies its own repeated-neighbor pairing and a proper four-coloring of the corresponding quotient.
claims.search_method: Exact composition of the independently verified equivalences in claims 0 and 1.

claims.claim: In particular, the target holds whenever some feasible pairing has a 3-degenerate quotient Q_P.
claims.evidence: A degeneracy deletion ordering, colored in reverse, gives Q_P a proper coloring with at most four colors because each inserted vertex has at most three already colored neighbors. Claim 1 then lifts it to the required coloring of G.

claims.claim: For a supplied coloring c, coarsenings of c are governed exactly by a color-constraint graph T_c.
claims.evidence: At every vertex the center color γ and the two neighborhood colors α,β are pairwise distinct. For a map f on old colors, f∘c is proper and still has exactly two neighborhood colors precisely when f(α), f(β), and f(γ) remain pairwise distinct. These are exactly the three edges of the corresponding triangle in T_c. Taking their union over all vertices proves the iff and the chromatic-number characterization.
claims.search_method: Direct local-constraint proof for arbitrary color maps.

claims.claim: A triangular prism has a valid three-coloring whose every local constraint triangle contains all three colors.
claims.evidence: The exact checker verified simplicity, cubicity, properness, the two-color neighborhood condition at all six vertices, and that all six local triples equal {0,1,2}.
claims.search_method: Direct exact verification of the six-vertex witness.

claims.claim: For every q≥3 there is a finite simple cubic graph with a valid q-coloring c such that T_c=K_q, although the graph itself has a valid three-coloring.
claims.evidence: For each three-subset {a,b,c}, one prism colored (a,b,c,b,c,a) is valid and contributes precisely its three constraint edges. Every pair of q colors belongs to a three-subset, so their union is K_q. The disjoint union is finite, simple, and cubic, and recoloring every prism (0,1,2,1,2,0) gives a valid three-coloring. Exact constructed instances q=3 through 12 also passed.
claims.search_method: Universal symbolic construction proof plus exact checks for q=3 through 12.
claims.witness: The disjoint union of one triangular prism for every three-subset of a q-color palette, with component pattern (a,b,c,b,c,a).

claims.claim: The coarsening obstruction already occurs in a connected 12-vertex graph: it has a valid six-coloring with T_c=K6 and also a non-coarsening valid four-coloring.
claims.evidence: The checker verified the adjacency is simple, cubic, and connected; both supplied colorings are valid; the six-coloring produces all 15 edges of K6; and the four-coloring is not constant on old color classes. It also exhaustively tested all 4^6 maps of the six old colors and found no valid coarsening.
claims.search_method: Exact witness verification and exhaustive enumeration of all 4^6 coarsening maps.

claims.claim: Four colors are genuinely necessary: K3,3 admits no valid coloring with at most three colors but has one with four.
claims.evidence: Properness in K3,3 forces the color sets on its two parts to be disjoint. Each vertex sees an entire opposite part, so validity forces each part to use exactly two colors, requiring four total. The checker found no valid map among all 3^6 maps into three labels and verified the four-color witness.
claims.search_method: Direct lower-bound proof and exhaustive exact search of 729 three-label maps.
claims.witness: On parts (0,1,2) and (3,4,5), the coloring (0,0,1,2,2,3) is valid.

claims.claim: For a cubic bipartite graph with parts A,B, a four-coloring using disjoint two-color palettes on A and B exists exactly when each part has a binary coloring that is nonmonochromatic on every opposite neighborhood.
claims.evidence: The union of the two binary maps is automatically proper because the palettes are disjoint. At a vertex in either part, its neighborhood has exactly two colors iff the binary map on the opposite part is nonmonochromatic there. Restriction of any separated-palette valid coloring proves the converse.
claims.search_method: Direct proof audit of construction and restriction.

claims.claim: Every cubic bipartite graph having a spanning 2-factor all of whose cycles have length divisible by four has a valid four-coloring.
claims.evidence: On a 4k-cycle, each bipartition subsequence has even length 2k and can be alternated with its side's two-color palette. The two factor-neighbors of every vertex are consecutive in the opposite subsequence and therefore have different colors; the remaining neighbor uses one of those same two palette colors. Disjoint side palettes ensure properness.

claims.claim: A further nonbipartite sufficient case holds: if M is a perfect matching, G−M consists of even cycles, and the multigraph obtained by contracting those cycles and retaining M is bipartite, then G has a valid four-coloring.
claims.evidence: Give contracted cycles on opposite sides of the bipartition disjoint two-color palettes and alternate around each even cycle. Cycle edges are proper, and bipartiteness ensures every matching edge joins different palettes. At each vertex its two cycle-neighbors share the within-cycle opposite color while its matching neighbor supplies one color from the other palette, yielding exactly two neighborhood colors.
claims.search_method: Direct proof audit, including matching loops and palette compatibility.

claims.claim: The full target holds for every finite simple cubic graph on at most eight vertices.
claims.evidence: The duplicate-free labeled generator chooses all missing higher-labeled neighbors of the least unsaturated vertex, which is the unique recursion path for every labeled graph. It generated 1, 70, and 19,355 graphs at orders 4, 6, and 8. Exhaustive pairing and quotient searches found respectively 0, 70, and 19,320 premise-positive graphs, all with four-color solutions; 33,767,294 pairing assignments were examined in total. Odd orders are excluded by handshake parity, order two cannot be cubic and simple, and the empty case is vacuous.
claims.search_method: Exhaustive labeled graph generation; exhaustive 3^n pairing assignments when needed; exact quotient four-color backtracking; direct checking of every lifted coloring.

target_evidence: The exact target asks for either a proof of the universal four-color conjecture or an explicit counterexample requiring more than four colors. The draft explicitly states that the conjecture is not settled and supplies neither endpoint. Its verified palette-free and quotient reformulations, obstruction to coarsening, sharp K3,3 lower bound, sufficient graph classes, and exhaustive result through eight vertices are correct and material but incomplete progress. Thus target coverage is VALID_PARTIAL_PROGRESS, and the draft's claimed_resolution of PARTIAL is ACCURATE rather than overstated or understated.
